proposals.rationale: 'Integrated defensive electronic countermeasures' is present verbatim and PE 0604270N (Electronic Warfare Development) owns it, but the announcement's own words defeat the attribution: this is 'the procurement of 284 full-rate production Lot VI' units. Full-rate production is by definition past the development line, and the name also collides with BLI 0576's 'Integrated Defensive Electronic Counter Measure (IDECM)' row. A development PE should not be credited with a production lot buy.

proposals.program_name: USN/USMC North Star Precision Approach Landing Capability (PALC)
proposals.announcement_evidence: the procurement, installation, test and delivery of up to 31 instrument landing systems (ILS) at Department of Navy installations in support of the precision approach landing capability
proposals.lexicon_quote: USN/USMC North Star Precision Approach Landing Capability (PALC)
proposals.rationale: 'Precision approach landing capability' appears verbatim, and BLI 2820 (Ashore ATC Equipment) owns it as 'USN/USMC North Star Precision Approach Landing Capability (PALC)' — the USN/USMC North Star prefix is the program office's fuller styling of the same designator, so this is an alias. The announcement pins the award to shore infrastructure — instrument landing systems comprising a localizer, glide slope, remote control status unit and distance measuring equipment, installed 'at Department of Navy installations' — which is precisely what an ashore air traffic control equipment line buys rather than an aircraft modification. Money agrees: 'Fiscal 2017 other procurement (Navy) funds', OPN being the appropriation BLI 2820 sits in (lexicon doc 333).

refute_a.reason: BLI 2820's own narrative carries a LANDING SYSTEMS section funding "Precision Approach Radars (PAR), Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) systems, Instrument Landing Systems (ILS), and other air navigation aids" and specifically "Instrument Landing Systems AN/GRN-33(V) will provide the Navy and Marine Corps with a self-contained Precision Landing capability at selected Air Stations" — the announced fiscal 2017 OPN buy of up to 31 shore ILS at Department of Navy installations is verbatim this 1810N line's own work, and PALC is a capability designator, not a platform the contract supports.

refute_b.reason: 0544 does own the bare string 'Precision Approach Landing Capability (PALC)', but that row is an E-2 Series aircraft line and the announcement is unambiguously shore equipment — 31 ground instrument landing systems with localizer, glide slope and DME installed 'at Department of Navy installations' — which only 2820's ashore ATC row can own; the JPALS rows at 2867/4213 name a different, GPS-based system.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the procurement, installation, test and delivery of up to 31 instrument landing systems (ILS) at Department of Navy installations in support of the precision approach landing capability
proposals.rationale: The competing half of the PALC name collision, recorded so the resolution is visible. BLI 0544 owns the bare name 'Precision Approach Landing Capability (PALC)' but sits under E-2 Series aircraft procurement — PALC there is an airborne modification to the E-2. This award installs ground-based instrument landing systems at shore installations, so it belongs to the ashore ATC equipment line and not to an E-2 modification line.

proposals.announcement_evidence: post-production engineering and logistics support for the T- 45 aircraft
proposals.rationale: Rejected under the section 3 generic-services and IDIQ patterns. The action is a ceiling increase on an indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for 'post-production engineering and logistics support' — the announcement states 'No funds will be obligated at the time of award; funds will be obligated on individual orders as they are issued', so there is no appropriation to attribute and no named program content beyond the airframe. The bare designator 'T-45' is also owned by two PEs in this org's index, 0569 (T-45 Series) and 0603208N (Training System Aircraft), and the aircraft here is the platform the support sustains rather than the line's own work.

proposals.announcement_evidence: This order procures 5,001 full rate production Laser Guided Training Rounds, as well as provides for the refurbishment of 1,667 metal containers required for shipping for the Navy.
proposals.rationale: As clean as this chunk gets. 'Laser Guided Training Rounds' appears verbatim and BLI 0160 (Practice Bombs) owns 'The Laser Guided Training Round (LGTR)' — the same name in the singular. The appropriation matches exactly: the announcement names 'Fiscal 2023 procurement of ammunition (Navy and Marine Corps) funds in the amount of $20,876,141', PANMC being the appropriation lexicon doc 338 covers, and the whole obligation lands there. The content is the line's own work — a full-rate production buy of the training rounds themselves plus shipping container refurbishment — not services, not a platform, and not a catch-all title. LGTR appears at no other PE in this org's index.

refute_a.reason: 100% fiscal 2023 procurement of ammunition (Navy and Marine Corps) against BLI 0160 in 1508N/PANMC, and the line's own narrative singles this item out — the munitions on the line are bought by Joint Munitions Command "with the exception of the Laser Guided Training Round, which is procured by NAVAIR", and NAVAIR Patuxent River is the announcement's contracting activity; the lake order obligates exactly $20,876,141, all of it a full-rate production buy of the line's own round.

refute_b.reason: 'The Laser Guided Training Round (LGTR)' is owned by 0160 alone in this index, the announcement uses the same name in the plural, and no other PE carries an LGTR or training-round name that this evidence could reach.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the procurement of aural cueing system and motion cueing system capabilities for the tactical operational flight trainer (TOFT) training systems in support of the F/A-18E/F and EA-18G
proposals.rationale: Rejected under the section 3 platform pattern. The designator 'F/A-18E/F' normalizes to BLI 0145's name 'FA-18E/F', but the announcement uses it only to say which aircraft the trainers represent — 'in support of the F/A-18E/F and EA-18G'. The award buys aural and motion cueing subsystems for tactical operational flight trainers, which are ground training devices; the aircraft procurement line buys airframes. TOFT itself appears nowhere in this org's index, so there is no correct owner to propose here.
